findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed house flies present in the kitchen near the triple sink. There was a bin of soiled wash cloths stored on the floor which seemed to be attracting the flies. Inspector suggests sealing soiled cloths in bags each night to prevent pest development. 

Inspector also observed a small swarm of gnats/drain flies present underneath the bar near the hand sink. The floors were damp and heavily soiled, which may be contributing to pest development. See violation #55 for floor cleaning details. 

A follow-up will be conducted on September 9th, 2025 to ensure the presence of pests has reduced and professional pest control has been conducted in the facility.

findings.comment:

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C). findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
Observed the sanitizer concentration at the bar sink to be 100 ppm. Employee stated formerly agreed upon procedure for setting up sanitizer sink. The bottle states to use 3 tablets in the sink. The addition of one tablet moved the 95 degree water to 200 ppm of available quat sanitizer. Reevaluate the current procedure and use a test strip regularly in order to verify that procedure is working as intended.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: Observed chicken thawing under running water in the 3 part sink during the afternoon break. Some of the chicken is not completely under the water. Use a larger container like a bus tub for holding the chicken during thawing. Kitchen staff will be back in less than 4 hours. Recommend that food in a process not be left unattended. 3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Sour cream is 50°F in the coffin cooler behind the bar. Ground beef is between frozen and 50°F on the prep table.  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was placed back into the upright cooler for proper thawing. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B). Do not thaw potentially hazardous foods this way as they can grow bacteria which can cause illness.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Observed two bags of ground beef (5 lbs each) to be thawing at room temperature. Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13. The beef was placed into the upright cooler.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures

Get the grease trap serviced and have a professional plumber clean out drain lines.
 
All water containing sewage shall be disposed of properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Top layers of sliced tomatoes and wrapped American cheese slices in the upper holding area of prep cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 47F-54F respectively. The products were discarded. Other potentially hazardous foods (PHF) in the top holding compartment had internal temperatures at 43F/below. Do not overfill pans in the top holding compartment of prep cooler. Also it is important to note, the top holding area is not typically intended for long term storage overnight (depending on the unit). If PHF is stored in the top holding area make sure products are at 41F/below prior to use, and keep foods in pans below fill lines to help keep foods at colder temperatures.  
Cold PHF shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41F/below at all times during storage.
**New prep cooler was purchased after December 2013 inspection**

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.160 - Stem thermometer most frequently used to check food temperatures and holding case were soiled with buildup. It was apparent the stem was not properly cleaned and sanitized after the last use, and the holding case had not been cleaned in quite some time. Bartender cleaned and sanitized the holding case and the stem thermometer during the inspection.
Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. Clean and sanitize the stem and holding case of the stem thermometer daily/as needed to help protect foods from potential contamination.
**Maintain a sanitizer solution just for the stem thermometer. Store a wiping cloth inside and use the wiping cloth to clean the steam before and after each temperature check. Up to every 4hrs properly wash, rinse, and sanitize the stem of the thermometer. Clean and sanitize the holding case as needed.**

Cleaned/sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 & 1310 - A) Gallon milk jugs under bar handsink had liquid inside. One jug was labeled cleaner, and two jugs were not labeled. Kitchen Manager stated the liquid was a type of window cleaner (Windex) brought from home by the owner in said jugs. Manager discarded all jugs at request of inspector. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law, and when possible left in original packaging. Use properly labeled spray bottles for the storage of all chemicals not in their original packaging. Properly label containers of toxic substances with the common name and use appropriate storage bottles.
B) Spray bottle of Windex and cans of Time Mist air freshener were on a small shelf above bottles of alcohol at the bar. Bottles of alcohol were moved to a different area for storage.
All toxic items must be properly stored separate from food and all food related items (i.e. clean equipment, single service articles), including bottles of alcohol, to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Chunky mold buildup was observed inside the ice machine at the juncture between the drip guard and the ceiling. A piece of black mold was observed on a piece of ice. The Bar manager cleaned the area in question, and a layer of ice was removed from the machine. Area that caused obvious cross contamination was corrected, but the entire ice machine needs to be serviced and thoroughly cleaned/sanitized. Food shall be protected at all time from potential contamination. **Get the ice machine serviced/cleaned before re-inspection in two weeks**

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text: 750.290 - Bottom inside blue ice scoop holder was soiled with old food debris (pieces of tater tots). Bar Manager setup bar 3 part sink and cleaned/sanitized the scoop and holder. Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. **Clean the ice scoop holder daily/as needed and maintain it clean to protect scoop and ice from potential contamination**

findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - A) (R) Paper towels were not available at bar handsink. Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing at all times. B) Bar handsink was soiled (food splash/general buildup). Maintain handsinks and all related fixtures clean. **Handsinks are to be used only for handwashing and for no other tasks.**

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - House flies (~9-10 total) were observed in the men's room, in kitchen by mopsink, at the bar, and around the front door/windows. Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized. **Fly swatters may be used as long as kill spots are immediately cleaned and sanitized after flies are swatted, and the swatter must be stored in an appropriate location (away from food, clean equipment, and single service items). Sticky fly papers/strips may also be used as long at they are placed in appropriate locations (i.e. by back door, next to mopsink, etc.).

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 (x2) A) Back door is not tight fitting around top and left side. Light was visible where gaps were present. B) Front door is not completely self-closing or tight fitting. Door sometimes sticks and gaps are then present around top/sides. Issues with doors may be contributing to current fly issue (see #35a). Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. Repair the doors so they are tight fitting, completely self-closing and vermin proof.
